narrative.text: General Brenner requests an audience in person rather than sending a memorandum, which is itself a kind of message. He arrives in full dress uniform for a meeting that did not require one.

Army Day falls in eleven days, Chancellor. Tradition calls for a parade through Ashenmere — armor, the honor guard, the air wing overhead. Halvek never missed one in twenty years. The men expect it. Morale expects it.

The men expect it. Not the nation — the men. Brenner has just told me, in the politest possible language, that the army answers to its own customs before it answers to my signature. This is not a request for a parade. It is a request to learn how much I will let him have.

Chancellor, a word before you decide. Tyvaren's border command reads every column of Veltrian armor as a message addressed to them, whether we intend one or not. A full parade this close to the frontier will not read as tradition in Tyvaren's briefing rooms. It will read as a threat.
Brenner watches you without expression, the particular stillness of a man who has already decided what your answer means about you, whichever answer you give.

choices.text: Approve it in full — armor, honor guard, air wing overhead. Give the General his tradition and let him report to his officers that the Chancellor understands the army.
Approve a modified parade — honor guard and veterans, no armor, no air wing. A commemoration, not a demonstration. Frame it publicly as fiscal restraint.
Refuse it. Army Day will be marked with a private ceremony at the war memorial — no armor in the capital's streets. Make clear the army parades when the Chancellor's office says it parades.
